question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Francois Martin — Foundation of Pondicherry and early bases]
options: Pondicherry (Puducherry) — Founded as a French trading post by Francois Martin in 1674, who developed it into the French headquarters
Valikandapuram — Governed by Sher Khan Lodi (vassal of the Bijapur Sultan), who granted the French the site that became Pondicherry
Surat — The site of the first French factory in India (1668), where Martin worked as an officer before his assignment to the east coast
Goa — Captured by Francois Martin from the Portuguese in 1680 to serve as the French western headquarters
wrong_fact: Francois Martin did NOT capture Goa. Goa was the stronghold and capital of Portuguese India, and it was never captured or occupied by the French. Francois Martin's territorial accomplishments and governorship were focused on the Coromandel coast (Pondicherry) and Bengal, not the Portuguese territories in Western India.
explanation: Francois Martin is regarded as the real founder of Pondicherry. In 1673, Bellanger de l'Espinay obtained the site from Sher Khan Lodi, the governor of Valikandapuram under the Sultan of Bijapur. Francois Martin took charge of the tiny settlement in 1674 and built Pondicherry into a thriving trading town. Before this, Martin had worked at the French factory in Surat (established in 1668 by Caron). Goa remained under Portuguese control throughout.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Francois Martin — Dutch conflicts and Bengal expansion]
options: Pondicherry (1693) — Captured by the Dutch fleet during the Nine Years' War, forcing Francois Martin to surrender the town
Treaty of Ryswick (1697) — International treaty that restored Pondicherry to the French East India Company
Chandernagore (Bengal) — French settlement established in 1690 on the Hooghly river under Martin's direction as Director-General
Masulipatnam — Martin captured this port city from the Kingdom of Golconda in 1685, making it a sovereign French territory
wrong_fact: Francois Martin did NOT capture Masulipatnam from Golconda, nor did he make it a sovereign French territory. Masulipatnam was a major trading port on the Andhra coast where the French had established a factory with trading privileges from the Sultan of Golconda, but they never claimed sovereignty or seized the city militarily.
explanation: During the Nine Years' War, the Dutch captured Pondicherry in 1693, and Martin was taken to Batavia. Pondicherry was restored to the French by the Treaty of Ryswick (1697), though the Dutch only handed it back to Martin in 1699. Martin also directed the establishment of Chandernagore in Bengal (1690) under a farman from Shaista Khan. Masulipatnam was merely a factory under the local ruler's sovereignty.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Francois Martin — Regional diplomacy and global career]
options: San Thome (Mylapore) — Captured by the French in 1672 but lost in 1674, which forced Martin to relocate the remaining French to Pondicherry
Banten (Java) — Port where Francois Martin served from 1665 to 1668, managing French trade in pepper and spices
Kaveripattinam — Martin obtained permission from Ekoji I (Maratha ruler of Tanjore) to establish a French factory here in 1675
Calicut (Kozhikode) — Martin personally led a naval siege to capture Calicut from the Zamorin in 1701, building Fort Saint-Louis there
wrong_fact: Francois Martin did NOT lead a siege to capture Calicut in 1701, nor did he build Fort Saint-Louis there. Fort Louis (Fort Saint-Louis) was actually built by Martin in Pondicherry (completed in the early 1700s) to protect the French headquarters. The French did not have a fort or territory at Calicut during Martin's life.
explanation: Francois Martin's early career with the French East India Company included service in Banten (Java) and Madagascar. In India, he was stationed at Masulipatnam and then Pondicherry. He was part of the French garrison at San Thome (Mylapore, Madras) under De la Haye, which was besieged and lost in 1674 to Golconda and the Dutch. Martin then moved the survivors to Pondicherry. He negotiated with Ekoji I of Tanjore for rights at Kaveripattinam. Fort Louis was constructed at Pondicherry, not Calicut.
